summary: This program builds a playlist as a List of Song objects, prints it in the order the songs were added, and then reorders the same list three times with the sort method: alphabetically by title, by energy level from high to low, and alphabetically by artist.

lines.text: A List is the right storage choice here because a playlist can hold the same song twice and cares about playback order, unlike a TreeSet or a Map.

Comparator.comparing builds the ordering rule from a single getter, and Song::getTitle is a method reference that names getTitle without calling it. The sort rearranges the elements of playlist in place rather than handing back a new list.
forEach is a shorter way to write the for-each loop used earlier, passing each song straight to println.
Use comparingInt when the field being compared is an int, so the value is compared as a number instead of being wrapped in an Integer object.
reversed() flips whichever comparator it is chained onto, which is how you get descending order without writing a separate comparison method.

Each sort call starts from whatever order the list is in at that moment, so this one takes the energy-sorted list and reorders it by artist; sorting is just a view for display and does not change which songs were added.
